description:
SILENT WRONG: `read(FH, ${$_[1]}, N)` -- the buffer a dereference of an @_ ELEMENT -- reads (the count is right) but never writes the buffer: the emission is (p-read (p-aref @_ 0) (p-cast-$ (p-aref @_ 1)) 5), and p-read writes back only through a buffer form it recognises.  `my $r = $_[1]; read($_[0], $$r, 5)` works, and so does `read($g, $$r, 3)` at top level.  PRE-EXISTING (base 5adcc156 identical).  Found by s513b while writing lib/autodie.pm (the read wrapper works around it through a copy of the reference).

  sub s2 { my $n = read($_[0], ${$_[1]}, 5); $n } open my $g, "<", $0; my $d; s2($g, \\$d); print "d=$d\n";
  perl: d=<5 chars>   PCL: d=

Check sysread / recv / the 4-arg forms for the same buffer-place gap.

=== DONE (s513f) ===
read / sysread / recv take their buffer through the macro %p-with-buffer-place: an element or deref place ($h{k}, $a[i], $r->{k}, ${$_[1]}) whose accessor returns the VALUE is read into a box holding its current value and written back through p-setf when the call answered a count (a place that evaluates to a box is used directly). Wider than filed: read into $h{x} / $a[i] / $r->{k} had never written anything either. Caveat: the place's container/key expressions are evaluated twice (read, then write-back). Guard Pl/t/misc-fixes-03.t row 5 (fails on main).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `read($fh, ${$_[1]}, N)` (buffer = a deref of an @_ element) never writes the buffer
